key_insight: Benign-looking instruction data can erode LLM safety, and gradient alignment can help identify which training examples contribute to unsafe behavior.
engineering_relevance: SimpleLoRIF makes gradient-based safety filtering practical for million-example post-training datasets while largely preserving model capability.
method: Simplify low-rank gradient attribution and restrict backpropagation to the final four transformer blocks.
Rank fine-tuning examples by gradient alignment with unsafe responses.
Create SafeTulu by removing the 20% of Tulu 3 examples most aligned with unsafe responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports emergent-misalignment detection AUC up to 0.865 and GCG attack success rate reductions up to 22% across Qwen, Llama, and Olmo, outperforming LLM-as-a-judge and prior gradient-based filtering.
watch_item: Reported gains do not establish universal safety; filtering effectiveness may depend on the unsafe-response probes, model, and evaluation attacks.
paper_title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
